source.title: Training Infinitely Deep and Wide Transformers
source.authors: Raphaël Barboni; M. D. de Hoop; Takashi Furuya; Gabriel Peyré

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a conditional convergence result for gradient flow in an infinite-depth, infinite-width transformer model. It does not test the listed benchmark, architecture, initialization, or learning-rate claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a theorem about gradient-flow convergence to a global minimizer under initial-loss and NTK-positivity assumptions. It reports no CIFAR results, classification-error measurements, or empirical training runs. Cited results and initialization examples are not extracted as study results.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence for an infinite-depth, infinite-width transformer under Wasserstein gradient flow. Its results do not test any listed version: it compares neither convolutional training errors, teacher-student widths, shortcuts, activation-matched initializations, learning-rate thresholds, nor normalization recipes. References to residual connections and Fixup provide context.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish well-posedness of training dynamics and conditional local convergence to a global minimizer. The guarantee requires suitable initialization-kernel positivity and sufficiently small initial loss; it does not establish the absence of spurious minima throughout the entire landscape.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical conditional Wasserstein gradient flow for a mean-field transformer; no benchmark training recipe or measured classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence depends on the initialization NTK lower bound and sufficiently small initial loss; the stated result is restricted to encoder-style, non-causal attention.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4 guarantees convergence and exponential decay of training risk when the initial V-derivative attention kernel has a positive integrated lower bound, the initial parameter second moment is bounded, and initial risk is sufficiently small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the specified mean-field encoder transformer, Wasserstein gradient flow converges to zero training risk from initializations satisfying a positive kernel bound and a sufficiently small initial-risk condition.

record.problems: The convergence guarantee is conditional and theoretical; it does not report empirical runs or classification-error outcomes. The authors also limit the analysis to encoder-style attention and fixed head dimension.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam, CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, and size, stopping, or regularization comparisons.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student training, spurious-minimum frequency, and the effect of extra student neurons.
All parts: depth-related training degradation, plain versus identity-shortcut networks, and the stated initialization exceptions.

All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, comparative training speed, and trainable depth. Initialization-kernel assumptions for transformers do not establish these effects.
All parts: finite learning rates, stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
All parts: normalization comparisons, accuracy gain per training time, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparative speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Section 3 gives attention-kernel injectivity criteria and positive and negative token-distribution examples. These concern applicability of the convergence guarantee; failure of a sufficient condition does not demonstrate failed training. None supplies a missing result on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, classification error, random or corrupted labels, and comparisons involving size, stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth comparisons, training error, and shortcut effects; the paper studies transformers and does not compare these conditions.
Comparisons of initialization methods, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth. FixUp is cited as context, not tested.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss increases or divergence, and sharpness during training.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed, accuracy, learning-rate tolerance, and FixUp performance.

rows.subject: Infinitely deep and wide mean-field Transformer
rows.size_stated: Infinite depth and infinitely many attention heads; head dimension fixed
rows.operation_detail: Theorem: gradient flow on the conditional Wasserstein parameter space, under an initialization condition.
rows.measure: Training risk along gradient flow and convergence to a global minimizer
rows.value: Theorem 4 states that ρt converges to ρ∞ and L(ρt) ≤ L(ρ0) exp(−C N⁻¹ λ₀ t) for all t ≥ 0.
rows.note: Conditional mathematical result; no empirical classification-error measure or CIFAR benchmark is reported.
rows.check: The theorem and its exponential risk bound are accurately recorded, but 'observed' cannot describe evidence for any listed version. This is a conditional mathematical guarantee, not an empirical training outcome; retain it only as a finding fitting no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Discusses residual connections, initialization and Fixup, but reports no test of V1–V6.

tranche.reason: Conditional convergence for mean-field transformers does not test any listed version. NTK positivity and small initial risk do not measure the specified initialization comparisons, training-error effects, or learning-rate dynamics.

source_check.notes: Theorem 4 matches the recorded convergence bound and initialization conditions. The guarantee is local in initialization; it does not establish absence of spurious minima throughout the landscape.
